brief: A 3D-printed PLA stepper-motor mounting plate, 120 mm long, 80 mm wide and 8 mm thick, with all four corners rounded to a 10 mm radius and a 1 mm chamfer round its top edge. On top, in the centre of the plate, a cylindrical boss 36 mm in diameter standing 6 mm proud of the plate, blended into it with a 2 mm fillet, so the part is 14 mm tall overall. A 22.5 mm bore through the boss and the plate, in the centre. Four 3.4 mm holes on a 31 mm square of centres, centred on the plate, for the motor. Six 4.5 mm holes equally spaced on a 56 mm bolt circle, centred on the plate. Four 5.5 mm corner holes on a 104 x 64 mm rectangle of centres, centred on the plate, each counterbored 10 mm in diameter and 4 mm deep from the top. Two 20 x 5 mm slots running along the plate's length, centred across the width, with their centres 14 mm from each end. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A flat 3D-printed PLA plate that mounts a stepper motor via a central boss/bore and NEMA-style bolt patterns, plus additional bolt-circle and corner mounting holes, used to carry the motor's shaft through a boss with no stated structural load.
stated: Overall plate: 120 mm long x 80 mm wide x 8 mm thick
All four corners rounded to 10 mm radius
1 mm chamfer round the top edge
Central cylindrical boss, 36 mm diameter, standing 6 mm proud of plate
Boss blended to plate with 2 mm fillet
Overall part height 14 mm (8 mm plate + 6 mm boss)
22.5 mm bore through boss and plate, centered
Four 3.4 mm holes on a 31 mm square pattern, centered on plate (motor mounting holes)
Six 4.5 mm holes equally spaced on a 56 mm bolt circle, centered on plate
Four 5.5 mm corner holes on a 104 x 64 mm rectangle of centers, centered on plate
Each of the four corner holes counterbored 10 mm diameter x 4 mm deep from the top
Two slots, 20 x 5 mm, running along the plate's length, centered across the width, with slot centers 14 mm from each end
Stated: carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Since it mounts a stepper motor via a bolt pattern and central bore, the plate needs a flat top mounting face to seat the motor flange
Since there is a through bore matching a shaft/coupler diameter of 22.5 mm, the boss likely needs to clear a rotating shaft or coupling without contact

Since four 3.4 mm holes are on a 31 mm square, this is inferred to correspond to a specific stepper motor frame size (commonly associated with NEMA-style motors), though the exact motor model is not stated
Since counterbores are specified 'from the top,' the corner holes are through-holes that allow bolt heads to sit flush or recessed on the top face
Since two slots run the length of the plate, they likely serve as adjustment or alternate mounting features, implying the plate may need to slide or be positioned relative to a mating structure

Since the brief states 'no load case,' the designer assumed the part's function is purely positional/mounting rather than load-transmitting, but this assumption is asserted by the brief rather than derived from any described duty cycle or environment
unstated: The specific stepper motor model/frame standard the 31 mm square pattern and 22.5 mm bore are meant to match
What the six 4.5 mm holes on the 56 mm bolt circle attach to (a separate mating part, bearing, or enclosure) and their angular starting orientation
What the four 5.5 mm corner holes with counterbores attach to, and what fastener (bolt type/head style) the 10 mm x 4 mm counterbore is sized for
The purpose and mating feature for the two 20 x 5 mm slots (what slides through or is clamped by them, and in which direction adjustment is needed)
Orientation/clocking requirement for the six-hole bolt circle relative to the four-hole motor pattern and the slots
Tolerances on all hole diameters, bore diameter, and the 36 mm boss diameter relevant to shaft/coupler fit or fastener clearance class
Surface finish or flatness requirement for the top mounting face where the motor seats
Operating environment (temperature, humidity, vibration, dust) relevant to PLA's known sensitivity to heat and creep

Whether the plate is meant to carry any dynamic or static force at all beyond its own weight, despite the brief's claim of 'no load case' -- e.g., motor torque reaction, vibration from operation, or mounting-induced preload from bolts
Fastener type/size for all hole groups (the hole diameters imply clearance for bolts, but the bolt size/class is not given)
PLA print orientation, layer adhesion direction, or infill requirements, which matter for a mounting feature subject to any torque or vibration
Whether the boss and bore are meant to support/center a bearing, coupler, or motor shaft, and what fit (clearance/press) is required there
Any surface treatment, color, or post-processing requirement
Quantity/reproducibility or tolerance stack-up requirements for mass production via 3D printing
risk_signals: Part mounts a motor with a rotating shaft passing through a central bore, which if undersized, misaligned, or if the boss fails, could create a pinch/contact hazard with moving machinery

Brief explicitly disclaims any load case ('it carries no load'), but the part is structural in function (holds a motor in position) and made of PLA, a material known to creep and soften at moderate temperatures -- if the motor generates heat or torque reaction forces in use, the disclaimer may not hold and this is asserted, not demonstrated, by the brief

assumptions.statement: The part is manufactured in PLA by 3D printing (FDM), as stated, with no additional grade, color or infill specification.

The four motor holes, six bolt-circle holes, four corner holes, central bore and two slots are all concentric/centred on the plate's geometric centre, with the slots running along the plate's long (120 mm) axis, and no specific angular clocking is required between the bolt-circle holes and the motor-hole square beyond 'equally spaced'.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives patterns 'centred on the plate' and 'equally spaced' but does not specify relative angular clocking between patterns.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a specific clocking relative to the motor pattern were required (e.g., for cable clearance or keying), the design would need rotation of the bolt-circle hole set, which is a simple, reversible change.

assumptions.statement: The 10 mm x 4 mm counterbores are sized for a standard socket-head cap screw to clear a nominal M5 bolt (5.5 mm clearance hole), with no specific fastener grade specified.
assumptions.rationale: 5.5 mm hole and 10 mm counterbore diameter are consistent with standard M5 SHCS clearance/counterbore dimensions.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a different fastener type or head style is intended, the counterbore diameter/depth may not provide correct head clearance or flushness, though the explicit 10 mm x 4 mm dimensions are already fixed by the brief regardless of fastener choice.

assumptions.statement: No specific tolerance class is applied to hole diameters, the bore, or the boss diameter beyond standard FDM printing tolerances; fits (e.g., shaft/coupler in the 22.5 mm bore) are assumed to be free/clearance fits, not press or precision fits.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives nominal dimensions only, with no tolerance or fit callouts.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a precision or press fit were required for the bore (e.g., for a bearing or coupler), the as-printed part may be loose or tight, requiring post-machining or reaming.

assumptions.statement: The part operates in an ordinary indoor, room-temperature, static-duty environment with no special humidity, chemical or UV exposure.
assumptions.rationale: No environmental conditions are stated, and nothing in the brief suggests harsh service.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: PLA degrades under heat, UV and humidity; if the actual environment is hotter or more exposed, the part could warp, creep or weaken over time.

unknowns.question: Does the 31 mm square hole pattern and 22.5 mm bore need to match a specific stepper motor frame standard (e.g., a particular NEMA size), and if so which one?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Confirms the mounting pattern and bore are dimensionally correct for the intended motor rather than coincidentally close; affects fit of the motor's shaft/pilot boss in the 22.5 mm bore.
unknowns.suggested_default: Treat the 31 mm square / 22.5 mm bore as the governing dimensions as given; no further standard lookup needed.

unknowns.question: What mates to the six 4.5 mm holes on the 56 mm bolt circle (an enclosure, a bearing retainer, a separate bracket), and does it require a specific angular start position relative to the motor holes?
unknowns.why_it_matters: If a specific clocking or mating part geometry is required, the hole pattern's starting angle matters for assembly interface, even though the brief only specifies 'equally spaced'.

unknowns.question: What do the two 20 x 5 mm slots engage with (a sliding clamp, a separate bracket, cable tie points), and is a particular sliding/adjustment range along the slot required beyond its stated 20 mm length?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Confirms whether the slots are purely for fastener/adjustment clearance as dimensioned, or need additional functional range not captured by the stated 20 x 5 mm size and 14 mm end offset.

document.name: Stepper motor mounting plate
document.description: Flat PLA plate with a central boss/bore for a stepper motor shaft, a NEMA-style 4-hole motor bolt pattern, a 6-hole bolt circle, four counterbored corner holes, and two length-wise adjustment slots.

interfaces.description: Central bore in boss/plate for motor shaft or coupler clearance; no stated fit class.
31 mm square NEMA-style motor bolt pattern, 4 holes.
56 mm bolt circle, 6 equally spaced holes, mating part unspecified.
104 x 64 mm corner mounting pattern, counterbored from top, mating fastener unspecified.
Top face of boss; intended motor flange seating reference.
